stem: In the inequality \(6 - kx < 2x - 10\), \(k\) is a constant. If the solution set of the inequality is \(x > 4\), what is the value of \(k\)?
solution: For the solution set to have the form \(x > \ldots\), the coefficient \(k + 2\) must be positive; then \(x > \frac{16}{k + 2}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This comes from a sign slip when collecting terms, writing \((-k - 2)x > 16\) and then solving \(-k - 2 = 4\); with \(k = -6\) the solution set is actually \(x < -4\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. With \(k = -2\) the \(x\)-terms cancel, leaving \(6 < -10\), which is never true: there is no solution at all.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This drops the 6 on the left side, so that \((k + 2)x > 10\); with \(k = \frac{1}{2}\) the solution set is actually \(x > 6.4\).
explanation.D: Correct. The inequality becomes \((k + 2)x > 16\); with \(k = 2\) this is \(4x > 16\), so \(x > 4\).

verify:
x = symbols('x')
target = Interval.open(4, oo)
ok = [c for c in choices if solve_univariate_inequality(6 - value(choices[c])*x < 2*x - 10, x, relational=False) == target]
assert ok == [answer]
assert value(choices[answer]) == 2
